To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the modification of the antibody Fc region to increase FcRn affinity resulted in a lower clearance and longer half‐life in monkeys.

the LS(Xtends) modification of an anti‐oncostatim M IgG1 monoconal antibody resulted in a lower systemic clearance, a longer terminal half life and a larger volume of distribution compared to the parent antibody in cynomolgous monkeys.

the modification of the human anti‐OSM mAb for higher affinity to the FcRn receptor resulted in lower systemic exposure and a longer terminal t1/2 in cynomologus monkeys, and that CNTO 1112 demonstrated linear pharmacokinetics in cynomolgous monkeys.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of novel anti‐inflammatory and anti‐cancer agents based on the use of oncostatin M, a pleiotropic cytokine that is produced by a variety of cells including macrophages, fibroblasts, and endothelial cells.
the pharmacokinetic (PK) evaluation of anti‐onco‐statin M (OSM), CNTO 111 and its Fc‐modified variant, CNTO 821, in cynomolguses.

the pharmacokinetics of anti‐OSM mAb and its Fc‐modified variant in cynomolgous monkeys, with the aim to provide a better understanding of the PK properties of the anti‐OSM antibody and to provide the PK data to predict human PK.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Fc region modification of the anti‐OSM mAb for higher affinity to FcR receptor resulted in lower systemic CL and a longer terminal T1/2 in cynomologus monkeys.
the LS(Xtends) mutation in the Fc region of CNTO 1219 resulted in higher affinity to the FcRn receptor and a significantly longer T1/2 in cynomologus monkeys.
CNTO 1118 is a human anti‐OSM monoclonal antibody, which is being evaluated for the treatment of osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, and psoriatic arthritis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Fc variant of anti‐OSM monoclonal antibody CNTO 111, CNTO 821, exhibited a 2.7 fold increase in half‐life in non‐human primates, and the PK parameters were used to predict the human PK parameters.
the modification of the human anti‐OSM mAb for higher binding affinity to FcR receptor and extension of half‐life in non‐human primates is an effective approach to develop a long‐acting antibody.

the Fc region of an anti‐oncostastin M IgG1 mab can be engineered to increase FcRn affinity and extend the half‐life of the antibody, and that the half‐life extension can be accurately predicted from preclinical data in cynomolgous monkeys.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LS(Xtends) modification in the Fc portion resulted in lower systemic CL and longer terminal half‐lives in cynomolgous monkeys.
the modification of the human Fc region of anti‐OSM monoclonal antibody for higher Fc‐Rn receptor binding affinity resulted in a longer terminal half life in cynomolgous monkeys.
the FcRn affinity of a mAb may be modified to increase its terminal half‐life without significantly affecting the systemic clearance in cynomolgous monkeys.
